held.title: rowsAffected==0 is treated as 'limit reached', which can wrongly reject existing devices
held.body: When the limit is reached, an existing device that was updated within the window can still give `RowsAffected()==0`. MySQL drivers often report changed rows instead of matched rows. If client_ip, user_agent and updated_at are all unchanged (for example two requests in the same second), the update affects 0 rows. The user then gets `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and is denied even though the device is already registered. Check whether the device exists before deciding the limit was hit, or enable matched-rows semantics for the MySQL DSN.
